# Source Dossier & Signal Analysis (Issue 105 — 2026-11-27)

Search Window Used: **30 days** (expanded to ensure primary-source verification and exact deadline/exhibition status confirmation across institutional announcements and research repositories).

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Proposed Title (CN)**: 俄亥俄州立大学诺尔顿建筑学院举办《Yeah, they were All Yellow》：从“亚洲、女性主义与建筑”的交汇处重构空间实践
* **Proposed Title (EN)**: Ohio State University Presents 'Yeah, they were All Yellow': Triangulating Asian Feminist Spatial Practices
* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Primary Source URL**: `https://www.archpaper.com/2026/11/yeah-they-were-all-yellow-asian-feminist-architectural-possibilities/`
* **Publication / Announcement Date**: November 18, 2026 (Exhibition opened November 2, 2026)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Curated by Ruo Jia (贾若), the exhibition opened at the Knowlton School of Architecture at The Ohio State University.
  * The exhibition centers on the three intersecting identifiers: "Asian," "Feminist," and "Architectural," addressing their historically understudied intersection in architectural discourse.
  * The physical installation features a custom grid of metal struts forming twelve structural nexuses, each associated with specific conceptual nouns (such as identity, absence, ornament).
  * The physical grid adapts to the gallery's structural C-beams and HVAC elements, creating an open framework for spatial conversation and production.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Connects feminist visual culture and spatial theory with East Asian identity, moving beyond theoretical speculation into concrete spatial and architectural exhibition design.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. No previous issue covered Ruo Jia or this exhibition at OSU.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Proposed Title (CN)**: 香格纳画廊呈现尹赟亚个展《暗流》：以自然物象与反射介质探讨凝视、时间与权力
* **Proposed Title (EN)**: ShanghART Gallery Presents Yin Yunya's Solo Exhibition 'Under Current': Examining Gaze, Time, and Power Through Reflective Media
* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Primary Source URL**: `https://ocula.com/art-galleries/shanghart-gallery/exhibitions/under-current/`
* **Publication / Announcement Date**: November 27, 2026 (Exhibition runs November 9 – December 26, 2026)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Artist Yin Yunya presents her solo show *Under Current* (暗流) at ShanghART's M50 space in Shanghai.
  * The exhibition spans photography, moving image, photograms, and physical installations.
  * Works draw from lunar phases, sea surfaces, seashells, ox horns, and conchs to analyze how time, history, and power sediment within natural and cultural objects.
  * Moving image works integrate reflective, mirror-like materials that turn the viewer's gaze back onto themselves, exposing the power dynamics and inequities inherent in looking.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Focuses on image critique, media materialities, gaze politics, and photogram/moving image practices in contemporary East Asian visual culture.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. First time covering Yin Yunya and this exhibition.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Proposed Title (CN)**: 国立历史博物馆开幕《从隐到显》：以 60 件馆藏呈现台湾女性艺术从被描摹对象到创作主体的演变
* **Proposed Title (EN)**: National Museum of History Opens 'From Hidden to Visible': 60 Collection Works Trace a Century of Taiwanese Women's Art
* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Primary Source URL**: `https://musa.guide/en/registry/exhibitions/69c04499b6034886987830e46a8c6718`
* **Publication / Announcement Date**: October 16, 2026 – January 17, 2027 (Highlighted in late-November 2026 exhibition reviews)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * The National Museum of History (国立历史博物馆) in Taipei is presenting *From Hidden to Visible: The Women of the NMH Collection*.
  * The exhibition gathers 60 works from the museum's permanent collection spanning over a century.
  * It traces the historical transition of Taiwanese women from passive subjects depicted in art to independent creative agents speaking in their own voice.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly examines institutional archival holdings, gender history, and the evolution of women's artistic labor in East Asia.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. National Museum of History (Taipei) and this specific collection exhibition have not been covered in the past 7 issues.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Proposed Title (CN)**: UIUC 团队评估并行子 Agent 机制：代码库生成性能微升 1%–5%，但 Token 成本飙升至 3.8 倍
* **Proposed Title (EN)**: UIUC Study Evaluates Parallel Subagents in Coding: 1–5% Benchmark Gain Costs Up to 3.8x Tokens
* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Primary Source URL**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33893`
* **Publication / Announcement Date**: November 25, 2026 (arXiv preprint v1)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Authors Zhiheng Lyu, Chengyu Yin, and Lingming Zhang from UIUC released the empirical study *When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction* (arXiv:2611.33893).
  * The study evaluated LLM-based coding agents (including Codex CLI and Claude Code) delegating repository-construction tasks to parallel subagents versus a single agent.
  * Findings show that delegating to subagents increased hidden test pass rates by only 1 to 5 percentage points while increasing token costs by 2.6 to 3.8 times.
  * On complex tasks, much of the performance gap was attributable to basic single-agent practices: extending self-checking duration, clean context resets, and splitting code into structured files.
* **Relevance to Muki**: High practical value for AI-native workflows and agent system architectures. Directly addresses Rule 9 by providing empirical evidence on cost efficiency vs. delegation overhead in developer/researcher AI workflows, steering clear of tool hype.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **Follow-up / Ongoing**. Extends recent coverage of AI agent workflows (VOL-Agent, EvoMem, HiVe-Mem) by evaluating multi-agent delegation overhead in software construction tasks.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Proposed Title (CN)**: 西弗吉尼亚大学图书馆启动 2027 驻留招募：聚焦“产业、劳动与社区”的档案开掘与艺术创作
* **Proposed Title (EN)**: West Virginia University Libraries Open Call for 2027 Residency: Archive Research on Industry, Labor, and Community
* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Primary Source URL**: `https://artistcommunities.org/directory/open-calls/call-proposals-wvu-air`
* **Publication / Announcement Date**: November 2026 (Application Deadline: November 30, 2026)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * West Virginia University Libraries launched the open call for its 2027 Artist in Residence (AIR) program, themed *Common Threads: Industry, Labor & Community*.
  * Selected practitioners (across visual arts, digital media, writing, book arts, and cultural heritage) will conduct archival research at the West Virginia & Regional History Center (WVRHC), examining union records, company town histories, oral histories, and community papers.
  * Support includes a $1,000 honorarium, supply funding, travel, lodging, and per diem for a 5–7 day residency in Morgantown, WV (March or April 2027), leading to an exhibition at the WVU Downtown Library and a public presentation.
  * Application deadline: November 30, 2026.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly aligns with interests in working-class history, archives, labor, and community-engaged media archaeology.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. No previous issue covered this residency call.
